about.title: Personal Injury Help in Los Angeles, California
about.longDescription: Few places put more people on the road than Los Angeles. The 101, the 5, the 110 and the 405 carry millions of trips a day, and the city's surface boulevards stay busy long after rush hour ends. That volume is reflected in the public record: in 2025 Los Angeles logged more than 12,000 injury collisions, leaving upward of 17,000 people hurt, with reported crashes tending to peak on Friday evenings. Behind those numbers are pedestrians, cyclists, motorcyclists and drivers whose lives changed in an instant — and many of them had no idea what their claim was worth or how little time California law gives them to act. LawProactive is a free service that connects injured people in Los Angeles with an independent personal injury attorney who knows how LA County claims and courts actually work. We are not a law firm; we match you with counsel and then stay out of the way. You pay no fee unless your case recovers compensation.

whyChoose.title: What Los Angeles injury victims should know

items.title: You generally have 2 years
items.desc: California usually gives you two years from the date of injury to file a personal injury lawsuit. On the region's busiest corridors, dashcam and traffic-camera footage can be overwritten within days, so acting early protects your claim.

items.title: Partial fault doesn't bar recovery
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault. Even if you were partly to blame for a wreck on the 405 or a surface street, you can still recover — your compensation is simply reduced by your share of fault.

items.title: No cap on pain and suffering
items.desc: In most California injury cases there is no cap on non-economic damages, so pain, suffering and loss of quality of life can be part of what you pursue.

items.title: Attorneys who know LA County
items.desc: Los Angeles claims move through the nation's largest county court system and involve insurers you'll see every day here. We connect you with counsel who handles these cases locally.

items.question: How long do I have to file a personal injury claim in Los Angeles?
items.answer: In most California cases you have two years from the date of injury to file a lawsuit. Claims against a public entity — a city bus, a dangerous public roadway — can carry a deadline as short as six months, so speak with an attorney quickly.

items.question: What if the accident was partly my fault?
items.answer: You can still recover. California uses pure comparative fault, so you may collect damages even if you were mostly to blame; your award is reduced by your percentage of fault rather than eliminated.

items.question: How much does it cost to talk to an attorney?
items.answer: The case review is free, and personal injury attorneys in our network work on contingency — no attorney fee unless they recover compensation for you.

items.question: Where do injury crashes cluster in Los Angeles?
items.answer: Based on reported-collision records for recent years, high-volume corridors include the US-101 (Ventura Freeway), the I-5 (Golden State Freeway) and the I-110 (Harbor Freeway), and reported crashes tend to peak on Friday evenings. These are counts from public records, not a judgment about any one road.

items.question: Do I have to go to court?
items.answer: Usually not. Most personal injury claims settle without a trial. Your attorney handles the negotiation with the insurer and only files suit or goes to court if a fair settlement can't be reached.
